what.text: The company is a leading non-banking financial company (NBFC) in India, providing a wide range of financial products and services. It focuses on financial inclusion and serves a significant portion of Indian households.

segments.name: Loans
segments.text: The company disburses various types of loans, including auto loans and loans against property. It serves both self-employed and salaried customers.

segments.name: Insurance
segments.text: The company offers insurance products as part of its financial services portfolio.

segments.name: Mutual Funds
segments.text: The company provides mutual fund products to its customers.

segments.name: Wealth Management
segments.text: The company is expanding its offerings to include wealth management services.

segments.name: Fixed Deposits
segments.text: The company offers fixed deposit products as part of its financial services.

snapshot.text: The dividend yield is low at 0.48%.

verdict.headline: Bajaj Finance shows strong revenue growth but struggles with cash flow and ROE targets.

narrative_vs_numbers.text: Management's narrative of strong growth is supported by significant revenue and profit increases. However, the negative cash flow and missed ROE target suggest underlying financial challenges.

bull.text: Bajaj Finance has shown significant revenue growth, increasing from ₹26,673 Cr in FY21 to ₹81,985 Cr in FY26.
Net profit has increased substantially from ₹4,420 Cr in FY21 to ₹19,332 Cr in FY26.
Quarterly revenue growth year on year was strong at 22.8% in Sep 2026.

bear.text: Cash from operations has been negative for the last five fiscal years, indicating potential liquidity issues.
Free cash flow was negative, reaching -₹66,686 Cr in FY26.
The reported ROE of 18.2% missed the management's guidance of 19% to 20%.
